sentences.zh: Programming Throwdown，第52期，科学Python。

sentences.en: Take it away, Patrick.
sentences.zh: 开始吧，Patrick。

sentences.en: Virtual reality.
sentences.zh: 虚拟现实。

sentences.en: When we're recording this podcast, we're, I think, just after the Game Developers Conference.
sentences.zh: 我们录制这期播客的时候，我想，应该是在游戏开发者大会之后不久。

sentences.en: And so there's been a lot of tech news buzz about virtual reality and all the cool, awesome demos people have of their games and projects that they're running virtual reality.
sentences.zh: 所以关于虚拟现实，以及人们展示的那些运行虚拟现实游戏的酷炫演示，有很多科技新闻热点。

sentences.en: So I thought this would be a good opportunity to talk about it.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这是一个谈论它的好机会。

sentences.en: But personally, I've never gotten the chance to use any of the new generation, the Vive or the, I guess, Sony has one now or the Oculus Rift.
sentences.zh: 但我个人还没机会使用任何新一代设备，比如Vive，或者我想现在索尼也有了一款，还有Oculus Rift。

sentences.en: But I hear it's a very awesome experience.
sentences.zh: 但我听说那是非常棒的体验。

sentences.en: And I'm starting to see, like, videos that make me excited to try it.
sentences.zh: 我开始看到一些让我很想尝试的视频了。

sentences.en: And I know it's virtual reality is always supposed to have been the next big thing for a while now.
sentences.zh: 我知道虚拟现实一直被认为是下一个大事件，已经有一段时间了。

sentences.en: But I feel like it might actually happen this time.
sentences.zh: 但我感觉这次它可能真的要实现了。

sentences.en: Or maybe it'll just fizzle and then they'll give up on it forever.
sentences.zh: 或者它可能只是昙花一现，然后人们就永远放弃它了。

sentences.en: Jason, have you tried, actually gotten to try any virtual reality headsets?
sentences.zh: Jason，你试过，或者说真的有机会尝试过任何虚拟现实头显吗？

sentences.en: I have.
sentences.zh: 我试过。

sentences.en: I tried the Oculus.
sentences.zh: 我试了Oculus。

sentences.en: It's pretty cool.
sentences.zh: 挺酷的。

sentences.en: One of the big things that I think I'm still waiting for, I mean, I'm obviously a huge gamer, right?
sentences.zh: 我认为我还在等待的一件大事是，我的意思是，我显然是个超级游戏玩家，对吧？

sentences.en: And so the gaming part of it, I think is cool.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得游戏部分很酷。

sentences.en: But what I really want is actually a way to, like, produce content, VR content.
sentences.zh: 但我真正想要的是一种能够制作内容，即VR内容的方法。

sentences.en: I mean, right now, almost all the content is synthetic.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，现在几乎所有的内容都是合成的。

sentences.en: It's all video games, you know, rendered.
sentences.zh: 全都是电子游戏，你知道，渲染出来的。

sentences.en: But it'd be amazing if, you know, you could just, like, set up a bunch of cameras in your living room and then, you know,
sentences.zh: 但如果，你知道，你能直接在客厅里架设一堆摄像头，然后，你知道，

sentences.en: put your newborn baby or toddler or something in the living room.
sentences.zh: 把你刚出生的宝宝或幼儿之类的放在客厅里，那该多棒啊。

sentences.en: And your parents could just kind of walk around, like, you know, they could, your parents would be maybe in, you know, Australia or something.
sentences.zh: 然后你的父母可以四处走动，比如，你知道，他们可能在，你知道，澳大利亚之类的地方。

sentences.en: But they could walk around the living room.
sentences.zh: 但他们可以在客厅里走动。

sentences.en: Does it require either, like, a robot or something like computational photography?
sentences.zh: 这需要机器人或者计算摄影之类的技术吗？

sentences.en: Like, you're taking a light field picture or whatever, some weird multi-camera pictures and then computationally adjusting for a virtual camera location?
sentences.zh: 比如，你拍摄一张光场照片或者其他什么奇怪的多摄像头照片，然后通过计算来调整虚拟摄像机的位置？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, what I'm envisioning is, like, what I envision is, like, you put a bunch of cameras in your living room and then they build, like,
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，我设想的是，我所设想的是，你在客厅里放一堆摄像头，然后它们构建出，比如，

sentences.en: a 3D representation of the living room, including, like, the table and everything.
sentences.zh: 一个客厅的3D表现，包括桌子和所有东西。

sentences.en: Yeah, I don't really know much about how that would actually work.
sentences.zh: 是的，我不太了解这到底是怎么运作的。

sentences.en: But, yeah, I'm sorry I'm, like, kind of making up the technology.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，很抱歉，我有点在瞎编这项技术。

sentences.en: But I just want the ability for the content to be real instead of synthetic.
sentences.zh: 但我只是希望内容能是真实的，而不是合成的。

sentences.en: So you tried the Oculus Rift, and one of the things about, at least I think, but currently about the Oculus Rift is it tracks where your head is, but you can't, like, like,
sentences.zh: 所以你试了Oculus Rift，我认为关于Oculus Rift的一点是，至少目前是这样，它能追踪你的头部位置，但你不能，比如，

sentences.en: if you get up and walk forward, it doesn't know you walked forward.
sentences.zh: 如果你起身向前走，它不知道你向前走了。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: Okay, and then the difference between the Vive, and I had to look it up, that's how it was pronounced, like, Vive, Vive, the HTC Vive,
sentences.zh: 好的，那么Vive的区别在于，我特意查了一下，发音是这样，Vive，Vive，HTC Vive，

sentences.en: is it actually has cameras in the room that track where you are.
sentences.zh: 是它实际上在房间里有摄像头来追踪你的位置。

sentences.en: So you can actually, like, lean, move, like, strafe left to strafe right, walk forward.
sentences.zh: 所以你实际上可以，比如，倾斜、移动，比如，向左平移、向右平移、向前走。

sentences.en: Oh, really?
sentences.zh: 哦，真的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, and then, like, it puts up, or at least in the demo I was seeing, like, it was putting up indications when you got close to your actual wall.
sentences.zh: 是的，然后，比如，它会显示，或者至少在我看到的演示中，当你靠近实际墙壁时，它会发出提示。

sentences.en: Like, you teach it the boundaries of your space.
sentences.zh: 比如，你教它你空间的边界。

sentences.en: Oh, so you don't run into the wall.
sentences.zh: 哦，这样你就不会撞到墙上了。

sentences.en: Yeah, because you can't see, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，因为你看不到，对吧？

sentences.en: Because it's not augmented reality, it's actual virtual reality.
sentences.zh: 因为它不是增强现实，而是真正的虚拟现实。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: And so I think that's kind of cool, but that's going to be a drastic change, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这很酷，但这将是一个巨大的改变，对吧？

sentences.en: Because, you know, I don't have as much time as I used to, but I remember being able to play for just hours and hours at a time.
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道，我没有以前那么多的时间了，但我记得曾经可以一次玩上好几个小时。

sentences.en: But if you're standing up, obviously, like, that would probably get tired because, let's face it, I don't think most gamers are in shape.
sentences.zh: 但如果你是站着的，显然，那可能会很累，因为说实话，我不认为大多数游戏玩家身体素质很好。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, there are other games, like, there's, you know, DDR, where you have to, like, you know, like, stomp on some foot pedals.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，还有其他游戏，比如，有，你知道，DDR（跳舞机），你必须，比如，你知道，比如，踩一些脚踏板。

sentences.en: There's the Wii.
sentences.zh: 还有Wii。

sentences.en: In the Wii, you kind of have to be standing.
sentences.zh: 在Wii里，你基本上得站着。

sentences.en: So, you know, I do think that, you know, there have been in the past games where you have to be pretty active.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我的确认为，你知道，过去确实有一些游戏需要你非常活跃。

sentences.en: But do people play them in the same amount of hours as, like, a Skyrim?
sentences.zh: 但人们会像玩《天际》那样玩上同样多的时间吗？

sentences.en: Oh, no, probably not, right?
sentences.zh: 哦，不，可能不会，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, maybe DDR, yeah, like, a very, very few amount of people over a long period.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，也许DDR会，是的，比如，极少数人在很长一段时间内会玩。

sentences.en: Yeah, DDR, I mean, I used to play DDR in college, and yeah, you really, you realistically can't play for more than an hour.
sentences.zh: 是的，DDR，我的意思是，我大学时常玩DDR，是的，你确实不可能玩超过一个小时。

sentences.en: You're totally exhausted.
sentences.zh: 你会彻底精疲力竭。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 哈。

sentences.en: Wait, were you good?
sentences.zh: 等等，你玩得好吗？

sentences.en: I was decent.
sentences.zh: 我还行。

sentences.en: I was terrible.
sentences.zh: 我烂透了。

sentences.en: I mean, given the amount of hours I played, I definitely wouldn't, like, let me put it this way.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，考虑到我玩的时间，我绝对不会，让我这样说吧。

sentences.en: I didn't have DDR talent, but I played so much that I could eventually beat most of the songs on the hardest difficulty.
sentences.zh: 我没有DDR天赋，但我玩得太多了，以至于最终能在最高难度下通关大多数歌曲。

sentences.en: Oh, wait, on the hardest difficulty?
sentences.zh: 哦，等等，在最高难度下？

sentences.en: I don't think I even ever have played, like, I think I never lasted more than 10 seconds or whatever the...
sentences.zh: 我觉得我甚至从来没玩过，比如，我觉得我从来没坚持超过10秒，或者不管那……

sentences.en: Remember Max 300?
sentences.zh: 记得《Max 300》吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不记得。

sentences.en: It was 300 beats per minute, and it was the fastest song.
sentences.zh: 那是每分钟300拍，是最快的歌。

sentences.en: I mean, now they have faster, but at the time it was the fastest song on the machine, on that version of the machine.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，现在有更快的了，但在当时那是机器上，在那版机器上最快的歌。

sentences.en: And I beat it on hard once.
sentences.zh: 我曾在困难模式下通关过一次。

sentences.en: It was sort of like my crowning DDR achievement.
sentences.zh: 那算是我的DDR巅峰成就了。

sentences.en: But, yeah, so I do this original.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，所以我做这个原创。

sentences.en: So will you be buying Oculus Rift after your demo?
sentences.zh: 那你体验过演示后会买Oculus Rift吗？

sentences.en: I definitely want to buy it.
sentences.zh: 我绝对想买。

sentences.en: It is $700, so that's something to think about.
sentences.zh: 它要700美元，所以这值得考虑。

sentences.en: But I thought it was amazing.
sentences.zh: 但我认为它太棒了。

sentences.en: I played this game where you're in a turret, and it was kind of, like, perfect for the Oculus Rift,
sentences.zh: 我玩了一个游戏，你在一个炮塔里，这简直是为Oculus Rift量身定做的，

sentences.en: because, you know, you're sitting in this turret, like this machine gun turret thing, and it can't move.
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道，你坐在那个炮塔里，就像那种机枪炮塔，它不能动。

sentences.en: It's just stationary.
sentences.zh: 它是静止的。

sentences.en: And it's sort of like Counter-Strike.
sentences.zh: 这有点像《反恐精英》。

sentences.en: Like, most shooting games, you kind of imagine, like, imagine, like,
sentences.zh: 比如，大多数射击游戏，你大概会想象，比如，想象，比如，

sentences.en: those time crisis and these games in the arcade where you have a gun and you're pointing it at the screen and shooting, right?
sentences.zh: 那些街机里的《死亡之屋》之类的游戏，你有一把枪，对着屏幕射击，对吧？

sentences.en: But in this case, it's kind of like Counter-Strike where you look around and it shoots in the middle of the screen, wherever that happens to be.
sentences.zh: 但在这种情况下，它有点像《反恐精英》，你环顾四周，它就在屏幕中间射击，无论那里是什么。

sentences.en: And so it was, like, a little bit of time kind of getting used to that.
sentences.zh: 所以，花了一点时间来适应那种方式。

sentences.en: But once I got used to it, it was awesome.
sentences.zh: 但一旦我适应了，它就太棒了。

sentences.en: I mean, it was a great experience.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那是一次很棒的体验。

sentences.en: I definitely would get one.
sentences.zh: 我绝对会买一个。

sentences.en: And if it was $300, I wouldn't even think about it.
sentences.zh: 如果它是300美元，我甚至都不会考虑。

sentences.en: But for $700, I wouldn't think about it.
sentences.zh: 但对于700美元，我不会考虑。

sentences.en: Well, and also, I mean, this is another one of the controversial things is that you need a beefy PC to play it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且，我的意思是，这是另一个有争议的事情，你需要一台强劲的电脑才能玩它。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's true.
sentences.zh: 是的，那是真的。

sentences.en: Because, like, I actually, I just upgraded my computer, not with the intention of VR, but just because it was getting so old, it couldn't function anymore.
sentences.zh: 因为，比如，我实际上，我刚升级了我的电脑，不是为了VR，只是因为它太老了，无法再运行了。

sentences.en: And so it's just coincidence that I do actually have the right specs for it.
sentences.zh: 所以这纯属巧合，我确实有合适的配置。

sentences.en: Oh, I do not.
sentences.zh: 哦，我没有。

sentences.en: Yeah, you have to have a, basically, you have to have a brand new computer.
sentences.zh: 是的，你必须有，基本上，你必须有一台全新的电脑。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So most of the demos seem to be first-person, but I saw a demo from Game Developers Conference for a third-person VR game where, like, you know, you ever played, like,
sentences.zh: 所以大多数演示似乎都是第一人称的，但我看到一个游戏开发者大会上的演示，是一个第三人称VR游戏，比如，你知道，你玩过，比如，

sentences.en: Metal Gear Solid, where you're, like, as you move into different, is it Metal Gear Solid?
sentences.zh: 《合金装备》吗，当你进入不同的，是《合金装备》吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, where, like, you're in a scene, almost like a security camera.
sentences.zh: 是的，就像你在一个场景里，几乎像个监控摄像头。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: And then you move into the next scene, and it kind of jumps, you know, and, except that you could kind of move the camera around with your head.
sentences.zh: 然后你进入下一个场景，它会跳转，你知道，除了你可以用头移动摄像机。

sentences.en: So your head was tracking the security camera or whatever, but it was a fantasy game, not a sci-fi game.
sentences.zh: 所以你的头在追踪监控摄像头之类的，但那是个奇幻游戏，不是科幻游戏。

sentences.en: And basically, like, you could pure, so your guy kind of starts on the left of the screen, and then he kind of runs in the room to the right,
sentences.zh: 基本上，比如，你可以纯粹，所以你的角色从屏幕左侧开始，然后他跑进右边的房间，

sentences.en: and you kind of have to track over to the right so you can still see him.
sentences.zh: 你得跟着向右转，这样你才能继续看到他。

sentences.en: I thought that was kind of a nifty excuse for, like, why you're not moving around.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是一个很巧妙的借口，解释为什么你不用四处走动。

sentences.en: Yeah, right, right.
sentences.zh: 是的，对，对。

sentences.en: That's cool.
sentences.zh: 那很酷。

sentences.en: Yeah, I wonder if, you know, if instead of you sort of, like, instead of the camera sort of being first-person, as you said, but instead, like, when you look around,
sentences.zh: 是的，我想知道，你知道，如果不是你，比如，不是摄像机是第一人称的，正如你所说，而是，比如，当你环顾四周时，

sentences.en: you actually orbit.
sentences.zh: 你实际上是在绕轨道运行。

sentences.en: So in other words, like, if I turn my head to the left, the camera actually just, like, swivels out.
sentences.zh: 所以换句话说，比如，如果我把头转向左边，摄像机实际上只是，比如，向外旋转。

sentences.en: I wonder if that would be disorienting.
sentences.zh: 我想知道那会不会让人感到迷失方向。

sentences.en: Yeah, it might be.
sentences.zh: 是的，可能会。

sentences.en: All right, well, I think we're on to the news.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我想我们该进入新闻环节了。

sentences.en: Yeah, news.
sentences.zh: 是的，新闻。

sentences.en: So the first news story I have is for all you students or teachers out there, I try and, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以第一个新闻故事是给你们所有学生或老师的，我尝试，你知道，

sentences.en: periodically give you good references for ways to sort of get some kind of free stuff.
sentences.zh: 定期给你们提供一些好的参考资料，告诉你们如何获得一些免费的东西。

sentences.en: And Amazon has something called AWS Educate.
sentences.zh: 亚马逊有一个叫AWS Educate的东西。

sentences.en: In the past, we've done GitHub.
sentences.zh: 过去我们做过GitHub。

sentences.en: There's a bunch of amazing free stuff you can get through them.
sentences.zh: 通过他们你可以获得很多很棒的免费东西。

sentences.en: We've done a variety of different sources.
sentences.zh: 我们做过各种不同的来源。

sentences.en: This one's pretty cool.
sentences.zh: 这个挺酷的。

sentences.en: It gives you $100 a year in free Amazon credit, which you can use to have a server running.
sentences.zh: 它每年给你100美元的免费亚马逊额度，你可以用来运行服务器。

sentences.en: That's right, web services credit.
sentences.zh: 没错，网络服务额度。

sentences.en: So you can use that to, you know, have your own server in the cloud running all day for a whole year for free.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以用它来，你知道，让你的云服务器全天候运行一整年，完全免费。

sentences.en: If you're an educator, if you're a teacher or something like that, you actually get $200 to share amongst your class.
sentences.zh: 如果你是教育工作者，如果你是老师之类的，你实际上可以获得200美元在班级里分享。

sentences.en: And it's really cool.
sentences.zh: 这真的很酷。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, $100 actually goes a very long way in AWS.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，100美元在AWS里其实非常耐用。

sentences.en: As I said, you can have a server running for a whole year.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，你可以让服务器运行一整年。

sentences.en: However, you could also do, like, there's something called Common Crawl, which is a data set that spans the entire internet.
sentences.zh: 然而，你也可以做，比如，有一个叫Common Crawl的东西，这是一个覆盖整个互联网的数据集。

sentences.en: So we've talked about this in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 所以我们过去谈过这个。

sentences.en: You can use Common Crawl to, like, see how many times, you know, Patrick shows up in the internet and just count all the Patrick's.
sentences.zh: 你可以使用Common Crawl来，比如，看看Patrick在互联网上出现了多少次，然后数数所有的Patrick。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: There's a lot of Patricks.
sentences.zh: 有很多Patrick。

sentences.en: They're not me.
sentences.zh: 他们不是我。

sentences.en: So, I don't even think I rank.
sentences.zh: 所以，我觉得我甚至排不上号。

sentences.en: You didn't even search my full name.
sentences.zh: 你甚至没搜我的全名。

sentences.en: I don't think I rank in Google.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我在谷歌上排不上名。

sentences.en: No, you don't have a Twitter account.
sentences.zh: 不，你没有Twitter账号。

sentences.en: How can you rank?
sentences.zh: 你怎么能排上名？

sentences.en: Do you have a Facebook or no?
sentences.zh: 你有Facebook吗，还是没有？

sentences.en: Does it count unused and I don't know the login and, yeah.
sentences.zh: 它算不算那些不用的，我不知道登录信息的，是的。

sentences.en: Okay, no.
sentences.zh: 好吧，没有。

sentences.en: Sort of.
sentences.zh: 算是吧。

sentences.en: You have a LinkedIn, right?
sentences.zh: 你有LinkedIn，对吧？

sentences.en: I applied to Facebook once and I thought it would be a good idea to have a Facebook account.
sentences.zh: 我曾经申请过Facebook，我觉得有个Facebook账号是个好主意。

sentences.en: Oh, that seems like a good idea, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，那听起来是个好主意，是的。

sentences.en: No, so I had one when they came out when you still had to be at specific universities and I was still in university.
sentences.zh: 不，所以我刚出来的时候有一个，那时候你还必须在特定的大学里，而我还在上大学。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And then I was like, nope, I actually don't want to relate to these people anymore.
sentences.zh: 然后我就想，不，我其实不想再和这些人有联系了。

sentences.en: So I closed it.
sentences.zh: 所以我把它关了。

sentences.en: That was before, like, it was anyone except college students.
sentences.zh: 那是在它还没被大学生以外的人使用之前。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And I think I'm remembering that correctly.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得我没记错。

sentences.en: Anyways, and then eventually, like, I went to recreate it and it turned out, like, I never, it's really hard to actually fully delete your Facebook account.
sentences.zh: 总之，后来我想重新启用它，结果发现，要彻底删除 Facebook 账号真的很难。

sentences.en: Oh, I see.
sentences.zh: 哦，我明白了。

sentences.en: And so it was, like, dormant or inactive or something and so it reactivated and I never bothered deactivating it again.
sentences.zh: 它当时处于休眠或不活跃状态，结果它又自动激活了，我也懒得再去停用它了。

sentences.en: So I, but I never go on there.
sentences.zh: 所以我虽然有账号，但我从不去用。

sentences.en: Got it, got it.
sentences.zh: 懂了，懂了。

sentences.en: I'm an antisocial person.
sentences.zh: 我是个不爱社交的人。

sentences.en: You would not show up that often.
sentences.zh: 你确实不怎么露面。

sentences.en: But, but, hey.
sentences.zh: 但是，嘿。

sentences.en: I one time used Google Plus.
sentences.zh: 我曾经用过 Google Plus。

sentences.en: One time.
sentences.zh: 就用过一次。

sentences.en: So scanning, you know, for all the Patricks and the whole internet, you have to scan all, you know, I think it's like 200 terabytes of data.
sentences.zh: 所以要扫描整个互联网上的所有 Patrick，你得扫描大约 200 TB 的数据。

sentences.en: And it only costs, I think, like $14.
sentences.zh: 而且费用大概只要 14 美元。

sentences.en: So you can see how, like, you have incredible computational resources at your disposal for free if you get this.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以看到，如果你能用上这个，你就能免费获得难以置信的计算资源。

sentences.en: So it's called AWS Educate.
sentences.zh: 它叫 AWS Educate。

sentences.en: If you're a student or a teacher, definitely go here, get your free credit and check it out.
sentences.zh: 如果你是学生或老师，一定要去看看，领取免费额度并体验一下。

sentences.en: It's awesome.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Awesome.
sentences.zh: 确实棒。

sentences.en: That's a good word.
sentences.zh: 这词用得好。

sentences.en: MAME went open source and the entire internet said, wait, wasn't it already open source?
sentences.zh: MAME 开源了，整个互联网都在说：等等，它不是早就开源了吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，确实如此。

sentences.en: But I think this is an interesting story and I put it in here, I guess, partly because of that.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这是一个有趣的故事，我把它放进来，大概也是因为这个原因。

sentences.en: And I know, Jason, you may have more context for this.
sentences.zh: 我知道，Jason，你可能对此有更多了解。

sentences.en: But when you get a bunch of people together and write code, there's actually a lot of legal implications whether you mean for there to be or not.
sentences.zh: 但当你召集一群人写代码时，无论你是否有意，都会涉及很多法律问题。

sentences.en: And who owns the code?
sentences.zh: 谁拥有这些代码？

sentences.en: Who has a right to the code?
sentences.zh: 谁拥有代码的使用权？

sentences.en: And these kinds of things are always very confusing and tricky.
sentences.zh: 这类事情总是非常令人困惑和棘手。

sentences.en: And the one I always remember isn't really related to code.
sentences.zh: 我一直记得的一个例子其实和代码无关。

sentences.en: I'm trying to remember now.
sentences.zh: 我正在努力回想。

sentences.en: I guess the guy who helped design the Stormtrooper helmet for the original Star Wars, like, it was unclear the manner, the contract and manner under which he got paid,
sentences.zh: 我想是那个参与设计《星球大战》原版帝国冲锋队头盔的人，当时他获得报酬的合同和方式并不明确，

sentences.en: whether he retained any licensing to the or any of the rights to Stormtrooper helmets.
sentences.zh: 他不确定自己是否保留了头盔的任何许可权或权利。

sentences.en: And so, like, he and Lucasfilm, I guess, or whoever owns the rights to Star Wars, like,
sentences.zh: 所以，他和卢卡斯影业，或者说拥有《星球大战》版权的人，

sentences.en: went back and forth with several lawsuits because he would make products or molds based off of those things that he made and claimed he had ownership to be able to do that.
sentences.zh: 进行了多次诉讼，因为他会根据自己制作的东西制造产品或模具，并声称自己拥有这样做的主权。

sentences.en: And they said he didn't.
sentences.zh: 而他们说他没有。

sentences.en: It just reminds me how, like, complicated – basically, if someone does work, whether you pay them or not for you and produces something, like, who owns the thing,
sentences.zh: 这让我想到，这有多复杂——基本上，如果有人为你工作并产出了东西，无论你是否付钱，谁拥有这个东西，

sentences.en: any copies of the thing, the likeness of the thing, if you don't nail it down, can get really confusing.
sentences.zh: 以及它的任何副本、它的肖像权，如果你不把它落实清楚，真的会变得非常混乱。

sentences.en: And that is sort of related, I think, to what happened in MAME is that people developed under different assumptions, different licenses, and then to change it,
sentences.zh: 我认为这和 MAME 发生的事情有点关系，人们在不同的假设和不同的许可下进行开发，然后要改变它，

sentences.en: you basically have to go back and get all of them to agree to it.
sentences.zh: 你基本上必须回去让所有人都同意才行。

sentences.en: That's right, and there's some parts of MAME.
sentences.zh: 没错，MAME 确实有部分代码是这样的。

sentences.en: I think it's actually the software scaler, if I want to remember correctly.
sentences.zh: 如果我没记错的话，应该是软件缩放器。

sentences.en: So, I'm a MAME developer.
sentences.zh: 我是 MAME 的开发者。

sentences.en: I've worked on it for a while.
sentences.zh: 我参与开发有一段时间了。

sentences.en: Actually, just a short tangent, I got a nastygram from PayPal today, and they said that basically it was from their brand integrity department.
sentences.zh: 其实，稍微跑个题，我今天收到了一封来自 PayPal 的警告信，基本上是来自他们的品牌诚信部门。

sentences.en: And so, I have a donate page on MAME Hub, which is a fork of MAME that I maintain.
sentences.zh: 我在 MAME Hub 上有一个捐赠页面，那是我维护的一个 MAME 分支。

sentences.en: And MAME Hub comes with a bunch of servers and infrastructure and everything, and so the donations just kind of keep the lights on.
sentences.zh: MAME Hub 附带了很多服务器和基础设施，所以捐款只是用来维持运营。

sentences.en: I don't actively work on it anymore, but there's still a community, and they maintain themselves financially through the donations.
sentences.zh: 我现在已经不怎么参与维护了，但社区还在，他们通过捐款在财务上维持运转。

sentences.en: So, PayPal basically said, look, anything having to do with emulators hurts our brand.
sentences.zh: PayPal 基本上说，听着，任何与模拟器有关的东西都会损害我们的品牌。

sentences.en: They don't want to be associated with it.
sentences.zh: 他们不想与此产生关联。

sentences.en: And so, they put my account in this sort of restricted mode where I couldn't do anything until I removed the donate button from my website.
sentences.zh: 于是，他们把我的账户设为限制模式，在我从网站上删除捐赠按钮之前，我什么都做不了。

sentences.en: So, in the email, they said, it's not illegal, like, what you're doing.
sentences.zh: 在邮件里，他们说，你做的事情并不违法。

sentences.en: We don't think it's illegal or anything.
sentences.zh: 我们不认为这违法什么的。

sentences.en: We just don't want to be associated with it.
sentences.zh: 我们只是不想与它扯上关系。

sentences.en: But is this a recent change?
sentences.zh: 但这是一种最近才有的改变吗？

sentences.en: Or they just recently figured out about you?
sentences.zh: 还是他们最近才发现你的存在？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, MAME Hub is reasonably popular.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，MAME Hub 还是挺受欢迎的。

sentences.en: I wouldn't say it's hugely popular, but, you know, it's been going on.
sentences.zh: 我不会说它非常火，但你知道，它已经运行很久了。

sentences.en: MAME Hub's been going on for about six years, and I've had the donate button almost the entire time.
sentences.zh: MAME Hub 已经运行了大约六年，而且我几乎一直都有那个捐赠按钮。

sentences.en: And, you know, I just got this nastygram today.
sentences.zh: 结果我今天就收到了这封警告信。

sentences.en: And it's not like the volume of donations has increased or anything.
sentences.zh: 而且捐款量并没有增加什么的。

sentences.en: Weird.
sentences.zh: 真奇怪。

sentences.en: Anyway, so, the software scaler in MAME is GPL licensed.
sentences.zh: 总之，MAME 中的软件缩放器是 GPL 许可的。

sentences.en: The person who wrote it wanted it to be GPL licensed.
sentences.zh: 编写它的人希望它是 GPL 许可的。

sentences.en: And so, I think even now, today, that is still under a GPL license.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为即使是今天，它仍然处于 GPL 许可下。

sentences.en: But everything else in MAME has been moved to BSD.
sentences.zh: 但 MAME 的其他部分都已经转为 BSD 许可了。

sentences.en: And as Patrick said, it literally came down to talking to every single contributor and getting them all to agree to change a license.
sentences.zh: 正如 Patrick 所说，这确实归结为必须与每一位贡献者沟通，并让他们都同意更改许可。

sentences.en: And so, it was free to download before, but there were restrictions upon, like, using it in commercial works.
sentences.zh: 所以，它以前是可以免费下载的，但对商业用途有限制。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It was not allowed to be used in commercial works.
sentences.zh: 它不允许用于商业作品。

sentences.en: And that's why, kind of a funny story, if you have a PS1, actually, or any PS, I guess, there was a PS1 game called Atari Arcade Classics.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么，有个有趣的轶事，如果你有 PS1，或者任何 PlayStation，有一款叫《雅达利街机经典》的 PS1 游戏。

sentences.en: And if you plug a keyboard into your PlayStation and hit Tab, you'll actually bring up the MAME debug menu.
sentences.zh: 如果你把键盘插到 PlayStation 上并按下 Tab 键，实际上会调出 MAME 的调试菜单。

sentences.en: So, it was, like, blatantly obvious that they were just forked MAME.
sentences.zh: 所以很明显，他们只是分叉了 MAME。

sentences.en: And they just built MAME for the PlayStation.
sentences.zh: 他们只是为 PlayStation 构建了 MAME。

sentences.en: And it turns out they did.
sentences.zh: 结果证明他们确实这么做了。

sentences.en: They worked a special license out with the MAME team.
sentences.zh: 他们与 MAME 团队协商了一个特殊的许可。

sentences.en: And so, a lot of people felt as if having that license forced Sony to pay us, like, pay MAME and set up an agreement to have a commercial, you know, fork of MAME.
sentences.zh: 所以很多人觉得，拥有那个许可迫使索尼向我们付费，也就是向 MAME 付费，并达成协议来获得一个商业版的 MAME 分支。

sentences.en: But the reality is, like, MAME is a pretty complicated beaSt.
sentences.zh: 但现实是，MAME 是一个相当复杂的庞然大物。

sentences.en: And so, to do something like compile MAME for the PlayStation, you need, like, a ton of expertise and guidance and consulting.
sentences.zh: 所以要像把 MAME 移植到 PlayStation 那样做，你需要大量的专业知识、指导和咨询。

sentences.en: And so, you know, making the license commercially compatible, you know, doesn't mean that, like, the project won't get funded anymore.
sentences.zh: 所以，让许可在商业上兼容，并不意味着项目就不会再获得资助了。

sentences.en: So, yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的。

sentences.en: So, you can do whatever you want with MAME now, commercially or otherwise.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以用 MAME 做任何你想做的事，无论是商业用途还是其他用途。

sentences.en: And that's a cool thing.
sentences.zh: 这是一件很酷的事情。

sentences.en: License is confusing.
sentences.zh: 许可协议真是令人困惑。

sentences.en: This is why lawyers make a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么律师能赚大钱。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: And this is why you should definitely, if you have anything to do with licensing, you should definitely have a lawyer involved.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么如果你涉及任何许可相关的事宜，一定要有律师参与。

sentences.en: And I think there are, which is called pro bono, like, working for free.
sentences.zh: 我想是有那种所谓的“公益服务”，也就是免费工作。

sentences.en: I think there are, I've seen stuff before from lawyers willing to, you know, help out with these kinds of open source things and questions around them.
sentences.zh: 我想我以前见过有律师愿意帮助处理这类开源项目及其相关问题。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I may be making that up, but I've never tried to seek their services.
sentences.zh: 我可能是瞎编的，但我从没试过寻求他们的服务。

sentences.en: And I don't know if those are people who you'd want their services or not.
sentences.zh: 我也不知道这些人是否是你想要寻求帮助的对象。

sentences.en: But I think I've seen it before.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我以前见过。

sentences.en: So, there's always something to consider as well.
sentences.zh: 所以，这总是值得考虑的。

sentences.en: I would like to talk a little bit about, this is, so this is going to be probably a little old by now, but I'm still really excited about it.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈这个，虽然现在可能有点过时了，但我仍然对此感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: And I actually tuned in and watched this.
sentences.zh: 我当时确实收看了直播。

sentences.en: I feel like it would, it's going to be momentous if it isn't already, which was AlphaGo playing the game of Go against Lee Sedol.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这具有划时代的意义，如果还没达到的话，那就是 AlphaGo 与李世石的围棋对弈。

sentences.en: Which most people agree has been dominant, if not the world champion for like about a decade and will go down as like a famous Go player.
sentences.zh: 大多数人都认为李世石在过去十年左右一直处于统治地位，即使不是世界冠军，也会作为著名的围棋选手载入史册。

sentences.en: And so, AlphaGo playing him was a big deal.
sentences.zh: 所以 AlphaGo 与他对弈是一件大事。

sentences.en: They were playing.
sentences.zh: 他们当时正在比赛。

sentences.en: But just so people know the context, so AlphaGo is a machine learning, an AI that was playing Go against Lee Sedol, who's a human being who was arguably the, one of the world,
sentences.zh: 为了让大家了解背景，AlphaGo 是一个机器学习人工智能，它正在与李世石对弈，李世石是一个人类，可以说是世界上顶尖的围棋选手之一。

sentences.en: one of the top world Go players.
sentences.zh: 世界顶尖的围棋选手之一。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And a computer was able to beat a person, was it four games to one?
sentences.zh: 电脑竟然能打败人类，是四比一吗？

sentences.en: Yep, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: So, they, interestingly, I don't know, I meant to look this up, but I don't know if it's the rules of Go or specifically here to avoid any funny business.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，我不知道，我本想查一下，但我不知道这是围棋规则还是为了避免任何猫腻。

sentences.en: That basically, they said, well, play five games is best of five, so three to win.
sentences.zh: 基本上他们说，五局三胜制。

sentences.en: But they said, even if a person or the computer reaches three games, they'll play all five regardless.
sentences.zh: 但他们说，即使人类或电脑先赢了三局，他们也会把五局全部下完。

sentences.en: And so, AlphaGo won the first three in a row, securing its victory for the entire thing with a million dollars on the line, which I think was put up by Google, who owns DeepMind,
sentences.zh: AlphaGo 连赢了前三局，锁定了整场比赛的胜利，奖金是一百万美元，我想这是由拥有 DeepMind 的谷歌提供的，

sentences.en: who wrote the AlphaGo program.
sentences.zh: DeepMind 编写了 AlphaGo 程序。

sentences.en: But they donated a million dollars to charity, but Lee Sedol would have won a million dollars if he had won.
sentences.zh: 他们把一百万美元捐给了慈善机构，但如果李世石赢了，他就能拿到那一百万美元。

sentences.en: But they won the first three, then Lee Sedol won the fourth one, and Google won, AlphaGo won the fifth one.
sentences.zh: 但他们赢了前三局，然后李世石赢了第四局，谷歌赢了，AlphaGo 赢了第五局。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And the interesting thing here, well, there's actually many interesting facts.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，实际上有很多有趣的事实。

sentences.en: So, one is that, you know, I tuned in live.
sentences.zh: 其中一点是，我看了直播。

sentences.en: So, it was live in Korea, which here on the West Coast was like late in the evening, like 8 p.m., 9 p.m.
sentences.zh: 比赛是在韩国进行的，在西海岸这边是深夜，大概晚上 8 点或 9 点。

sentences.en: Go games last a pretty long time, apparently.
sentences.zh: 显然围棋比赛持续的时间相当长。

sentences.en: That was definitely up till 2 a.m.
sentences.zh: 那场比赛绝对一直下到了凌晨 2 点。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: But the commentary they had, you know, they did, in America, Go isn't very big.
sentences.zh: 但他们的解说，你知道，在美国，围棋并不是很流行。

sentences.en: But everywhere else, well, in Asia, I guess, several countries in Asia, China, Korea, and I think Japan is pretty big, like really big.
sentences.zh: 但在其他地方，在亚洲，中国、韩国，我想日本也很流行，非常流行。

sentences.en: And so, they're actually paid professionals playing Go.
sentences.zh: 所以有职业棋手在下围棋。

sentences.en: And so, they had commentators there.
sentences.zh: 他们有解说员。

sentences.en: They had like a press room around it.
sentences.zh: 周围还有新闻发布室。

sentences.en: And they had commentary in English that I watched on the West CoaSt.
sentences.zh: 我在西海岸看了英语解说。

sentences.en: And I thought it was just awesome to like watch it live, even though it was kind of weird, like seemed kind of nerdy.
sentences.zh: 我觉得能看直播真是太棒了，尽管这看起来有点奇怪，甚至有点书呆子气。

sentences.en: But I feel like I've always read about Kasparov and Deep Blue.
sentences.zh: 但我感觉我一直读到关于卡斯帕罗夫和深蓝的故事。

sentences.en: And I felt like this was happening again.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这又在重演。

sentences.en: And I wanted to like say I watched it live.
sentences.zh: 我想说我看了直播。

sentences.en: Yeah, it was amazing.
sentences.zh: 是的，太神奇了。

sentences.en: Just a few like things to note.
sentences.zh: 有几点值得注意。

sentences.en: So, Lisa et al., he gave a lot of commentary about, you know, the games and everything.
sentences.zh: 李世石对比赛发表了很多评论。

sentences.en: And a few things he mentioned, which I thought were fascinating and makes sense when you think about it, is, you know, humans, you know, they pursue one initiative at a time.
sentences.zh: 他提到的一些事情我觉得很迷人，而且仔细想想也很有道理，那就是人类一次只追求一个目标。

sentences.en: So, you know, a human might concentrate on one area of the board.
sentences.zh: 所以人类可能会专注于棋盘的一个区域。

sentences.en: And there's sort of this agreement, like, I mean, not officially, but, you know, if I place a stone on the bottom left,
sentences.zh: 这有一种默契，不是官方的，但如果我在左下角放一颗棋子，

sentences.en: and there's some battle going on in the bottom left of the board, that's going to draw the attention of my opponent.
sentences.zh: 棋盘左下角正在进行某种战斗，那会吸引我对手的注意。

sentences.en: And he's going to place a stone there.
sentences.zh: 他也会在那里放一颗棋子。

sentences.en: And then we're going to have a little battle on the bottom left of the board.
sentences.zh: 然后我们会在棋盘左下角进行一场小规模的战斗。

sentences.en: But when you're playing against AlphaGo, it doesn't really care about what happened last move.
